chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Everything is to perish except His face.' He said: Whoever comes to Allah with what He commanded in terms of obeying Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), he is the 'face' that will not perish. And similarly He said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah.'

key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: His Face (referring to the enduring reality of obedience to the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What does the 'Face of God' refer to in Shia interpretation of Surah Qasas 28:88?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets 'His Face' (Wajh) not as a physical attribute but as the enduring reality of divine command embodied in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). This interpretation aligns with the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* by emphasizing that true permanence lies in obedience to the Prophet, who serves as the living manifestation of God's will. The hadith reinforces the inseparable link between obeying the Messenger and obeying Allah, as stated in Surah An-Nisa.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/332] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr from Safwan al-Jammal from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “Everything is to perish except His face” [28:88].

He said: Whoever comes to Allah with what he had been ordered (to do) in terms of obeying Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله then he is the ‘face’ who will not perish. In a similar vein Did He say: “whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah” [4:80].
